evidence.claim: Past alerts on this device profile were mostly cleared (CC-0487, CC-1447), e.g. customers confirming purchases from new phones — bank memory: 10% of 145 past model alerts with this signal were fraud (vs 35% without)

Device profile marked New for this account (Trident/7.0 | Windows 10 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080) and never seen on the card before — bank memory: less alarming than it looks: 8% of 577 past model alerts with this signal were fraud (vs 63% without), so here it counts towards a genuine customer
Bank model scored the transaction 0.52 (treated as a weak input: above 0.7 most alerts are legitimate)

Retrieved guidance applied: Card-not-present fraud: the card number is used online without the card, with amounts and products that do not fit the cardholder's history, often a burst of two to four within 48 hours. One unusual online purchase alone is ambiguous and should be verified.

case.summary: The transaction of $125.08 was reviewed and allowed, and the case was closed as legitimate. Evidence showed the device profile was new but only 8% of similar alerts were fraud and past alerts on that device were mostly cleared, indicating a genuine customer. The model score of 0.52 was a weak input and did not constitute an adverse signal. Because the fraud probability was low (0.05) and the evidence supported legitimacy, the card was not blocked and the case was closed without fraud.
